gh-issue-3084 (reject NAT64 + SIIT IPv4-in-IPv6 SSRF embeddings; follow-up chain #3079->#3082->#3084) merged 10-15. Fix is CORRECT and well-placed: new embedded_ipv4() helper in common/url_validation.rs extracts the low-32-bit IPv4 for the NAT64 well-known prefix 64:ff9b::/96 (RFC 6052) and SIIT/IPv4-translated ::ffff:0:0/96, both of which to_ipv4()/to_ipv4_mapped() leave uncanonicalised, and it sits INSIDE is_forbidden_ip -- which is reached by both the literal-IP arm (lines 162/167) and the DNS-re-resolution path validate_resolved_addrs (line 233), so a hostname resolving to such an embedding is caught too. 2 regression tests added (rejects_nat64_metadata, rejects_siit_translated_loopback). 1 LOW security finding -> issue #3099: is_nat64_well_known hard-codes segs[0..6] to the exact well-known value (segs[2]==0 ... segs[5]==0) so it matches ONLY 64:ff9b::/96; the RFC 8215 local-use NAT64 prefix 64:ff9b:1::/48 is still uncovered (64:ff9b:1:...::169.254.169.254 would reach metadata on a host running NAT64 on the local-use prefix). Lower likelihood (needs that NAT64 egress config). Proposal: extend embedded_ipv4 to match segs[0]==0x0064 && segs[1]==0xff9b && segs[2]==0x0001 for the /96-on-local-use case (low 32 bits), noting shorter prefixes need the full RFC 6052 section 2.2 interleaved extraction across the u-octet; add regression cases. Operator-specific NSPs left out of scope (not enumerable) -- correct scoping.

code-review-reality-server-dup-url-validator merged 10-13: dedups SSRF validator by deleting reality-server util/url_validator.rs (validate_fetch_url) + its 350 lines of tests and switching agency_imports.rs to common::url_validation::validate_external_url. Consolidation is the right move — the shared validator is STRICTLY more comprehensive (CGNAT 100.64/10, documentation ranges, blocked cloud-metadata hostnames metadata.google.internal/169.254.169.254, .local/.internal TLDs, plus the validate_resolved_host/validate_resolved_addrs DNS-re-resolution layer the local one never had). 1 LOW security finding -> issue #3079: the IPv6 arm of is_forbidden_ip (common/src/url_validation.rs) uses to_ipv4_mapped() which only unmaps the ::ffff: form, whereas the DELETED validator used to_ipv4() which also unmaps the deprecated IPv4-COMPATIBLE form (::a.b.c.d). So a literal ::127.0.0.1 / ::169.254.169.254 (compatible form) now returns Ok from the static check where reality-server previously rejected it — a narrow (deprecated-address-class, literal-IP-only) SSRF-filter regression introduced by the dedup. Proposal: in the V6 arm fall back to v6.to_ipv4() when to_ipv4_mapped() is None (guarding ::/::1) and run check_ipv4; add regression cases for ::127.0.0.1 and ::169.254.169.254. The reports.rs/users.rs XSS image/link validators were intentionally left inlined (distinct concern) — correct scoping, not a finding.
